note: Every host the browser code can request (discovered by scripts/outbound-hosts.mjs from string and template literals — never from comments), with what it is asked for, what it is SENT, and the words of Privacy §4 (js/legal-text.js, en AND jp) that say so. A host that is only ever a link carries `link` with the reason instead. `npm run check:datagov` (rule outbound-disclosed) fails on a requested host missing here, on disclosure words absent from either language, and on a row whose host the code no longer requests. This is a statement of fact about the code, not an exemption: adding a row without the policy saying it is impossible.
